title: Paris 1481 (Missale Parisiense): complete strict Canon Missae constituent — independent pixel-collation review
scope: Complete strict Eucharistic Canon of the 22 September 1481 Paris-use missal printed by Jean Dupré and Didier Huym (BSG OEXV 228 RES, PDF pp. 180-182, including printed fol. lxxx at PDF p. 181): from the opening rubric Junctis manibus se inclinet ante altare. and illuminated Te igitur on PDF p. 180 col. 1 through notated Per omnia secula seculorum. Amen. on PDF p. 182 col. 2 immediately before Oremus. Preceptis salutaribus / Pater noster. Includes all printed action rubrics and 25 illuminated crosses (✠) under declared selective Latin reading normalization.
method: Independent pixel-level visual inspection of all rendered facsimile pages by independent-collator-v3-alex-west (distinct from drafter AI source transcriber (Lane T3, direct PNG inspection of Paris 1481 PDF pp. 180-182)) on 2026-11-25. Applied 28 pixel-verified correction(s) relative to initial draft; verified every unit boundary, page account (1..506), and SHA-256 hash.
normalization_limit: Direct reading from 200-dpi rendered PNG images (and tight column zooms) of Paris 1481 PDF pp. 180-182. UTF-8 NFC, LF line endings. Standard 15th-century Gothic Latin abbreviations expanded silently to reading forms (nasal macrons, -q3 -> -que, -b3 -> -bus, -9 -> -us, Tironian ⁊ -> et, ꝝ -> -rum, dñs/dñi/dñm -> dominus/domini/dominum, nr̃m/nr̃os -> nostrum/nostros, oĩbus/oĩpotẽtem -> omnibus/omnipotentem, sãctas/sctĩ -> sanctas/sancti, eĩ -> enim, ĩpm -> ipsum, p̃claram/p̃stas -> preclaram/prestas, q̃d -> quod, s3 -> sed, p̃/ꝓ -> pro, grã -> gratia, cõcedas -> concedas, ɔspectu -> conspectu). Long s normalized to s; illuminated display initials merged with word bodies (restoring faded red/pink initials visible as coloured washes); line wraps and line-end hyphens joined. Medieval Latin orthography preserved verbatim (e for ae/oe: hec, que, celum, eterni, preclare, uenie; u/v as printed (Gothic word-initial v / medial u): viuo, vero, vultu, venie, eleuatis, serui; circumastantium, Imprimis, Symonis, Mathei, Thadei, Sixti, Crisogoni, propicio, imaculatam, tereritis, Et quequot, loco refrigerii, Ignacio). Action rubrics occupy separate lines within the Canon unit they govern; red/blue crosses serialized as ✠ (25 crosses total). Chant pitches excluded.
review_limit: Complete declared constituent only, not whole-book transcription or diplomatic typography.
